os_version: Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12.95+deb13-amd64, headless server — Chrome headed under Xvfb 1280x800 (X11)
app: Blind navigation on 5 live sites in Chromium 148 (Hacker News, Wikipedia, GitHub, MDN, DuckDuckGo) — Linux confirmation run of the macOS cell
channel_setup: Same Chrome-under-Xvfb + hardened distiller as linux-web-battery-cdp, viewport 1280x800 CSS. Same router and steps as macOS (campaign/linux/web-navigate.mjs, paths-only diff): every decision — which line to target, where to click, whether to refuse — is taken from the published view lines alone. No screenshot is read anywhere in the loop; screenshots are taken after each step only as evidence.

t1_read_text.detail: Targets located by text in the structured view on all steps that had one, first view except the deliberate below-the-fold step.

t2_enumerate.detail: The geometric text→control join (smallest interactive box containing the matched text's centre) worked on every step, including reading the affordance off the joined tag: <a> → navigate, <summary> → toggle. Wikipedia's 'Rasterization' had exactly one un-occluded candidate in view; the router picked it without disambiguation logic.

t3_live_value.detail: No form filled on third-party sites (read-only discipline).

t4_living_screen.detail: Not applicable to a navigation probe.

t5_blind_action.detail: 8/8 steps, first attempt each: 6/6 navigate (HN 'new' → /newest; Wikipedia in-article 'Rasterization' → #Rasterization anchor; GitHub 'Insights' on the hydrated app shell → /pulse; MDN sidebar 'Canvas tutorial' → /Canvas_API/Tutorial; DuckDuckGo 'Images' filter → &ia=images; HN 'More' below the fold → /?p=2 after one 90%-viewport scroll), 1/1 toggle (MDN 'Tutorial' disclosure widget), 1/1 correct refusal (no 'Pull requests' tab offered on torvalds/linux, where PRs are disabled — the negative control).

t6_pictorial.detail: No pictorial target was aimed at.

measurements.notes: SESSION COST: 16654 structured tokens across 9 view reads vs 12294 for 9 CSS-resolution screenshots — structured 1.35x MORE expensive (macOS: 16826 vs 12294, 1.37x). Same honest conclusion: at CSS resolution on these text-bearing pages the structured route costs more per look; it flips decisively at Retina/high-DPI (4784 tokens per 2x screenshot). SCROLL-AND-SEARCH replicated: the HN 'More' target needed 2 views (1 scroll), exactly as on macOS. THE DETERMINISM DETAIL WORTH PUBLISHING: the MDN disclosure toggle changed the structured view by +16 lines — the SAME +16 lines as on macOS, on a different OS, CPU architecture and Chromium major (148 vs 151), two days apart. The channel did not just agree qualitatively; the in-channel effect of the same action on the same page is byte-countably identical. The toggle step again needed no screenshot to confirm its own effect: URL unchanged, view changed — self-verification inside the channel. Router logic (the text→control geometric join, affordance read off the tag, absent-as-first-class-expectation) transferred with zero Linux-specific modification, which is the point of a browser-level channel: the router is OS-invariant.

runtime_verification.method: Outcome judged by the browser's own resulting URL and title (not by the view that chose the click), plus a post-click screenshot per step kept under nav-shots/.
runtime_verification.agreement: 8/8. URLs land exactly where the macOS run landed (same /newest, /pulse, #Rasterization, /Canvas_API/Tutorial, &ia=images, /?p=2). The toggle's +16-line view delta doubles as a cross-OS determinism check against the macOS value.

permissions_required: None (loopback CDP socket). No login on any site.
agent: claude-code (Fable 5) on debian-server (headless), Chrome under Xvfb
